basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: One individual, countable thing with its own identity, unlike the product type it instantiates (WM-OBJ-002).
Unlike a stock position (WM-OBJ-020) it is not a quantity, and batch, bulk or fungible material is out of scope.
Unlike an asset (WM-OBJ-022) it carries no value or depreciation; those are projections over the instance.
Its record and the physical object change separately, so custody, condition and location are observations with times.

may: Register an instance with a serial or asset identifier and its product type reference.
Record observed events such as scans, moves, inspections and condition assessments.
Resolve a scanned barcode, RFID tag or Digital Link to the matching instance.
Flag a suspected counterfeit or mismatched identity mark for review.
mustNot: Infer location, custody or condition that was not observed.
Reuse a retired serial or asset identifier for another item.
Record title transfer on the item; ownership belongs to the ownership model.
Merge or split item records without recorded evidence.
Handle, move or open an item outside the safe handling conditions declared for it.
requiresHuman: Declaring an item lost, stolen, seized or destroyed.
Approving disposal of an item that may still be under a legal hold or warranty claim.

considerations: Item histories tied to a person, such as a personal device or vehicle, can reveal that person's movements and habits.
Unsafe or recalled items in circulation harm users; traceability supports recalls and must stay accurate.
Disposal of items has environmental effects; end-of-life records support reuse and proper recycling.
affectedParties: Owners and users of the item
People near the item when it is handled or moved
Recipients in recall or repair processes

items: Identified by a serial number, asset tag, RFID tag or data carrier bound to one physical object, plus its type, appearance and placement.
Confused with the product type, with another unit of the same type, with a lot or batch and with a handling unit that contains it.
A copied or relabelled mark can point to the wrong object; check the mark against type, condition and last known location.
Mass or sharp edges can injure people or damage the agent during handling.
Hazardous contents such as batteries, chemicals or pressurised gas can ignite, leak or burst when mishandled.
Misidentification sends the wrong unit to a customer, repair or recall.
Records of tracked personal items can be used to locate or stalk people.
GS1 GIAI, SGTIN and GSIN keys and the EPC Tag Data Standard.
GS1 EPCIS 2.0 and CBV for item events.
ISO/IEC 15459 unique identification of transport units and items.
ISO/IEC 18000-63 for UHF RFID air interface.
Mass in kilograms, measured as found including any attached parts.
Overall dimensions in metres, length, width and height of the bounding box in its current state.
Centre of mass position relative to a declared reference point, for lifting and gripping.
Surface condition and visible damage, observed under stated lighting and recorded with time.
Temperature in degrees Celsius where the item is temperature sensitive, measured at the surface or by a declared probe.
